newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker seeks large savings on air bills.
newsitem.headline: Schenker seeks large savings on air bills.

text.p: Global freight forwarder Schenker International said millions of dollars can be saved in air cargo customer costs by improved airline billing checks.
Schenker International (SI) will introduce a uniform worldwide quality standard based on its "Airline Billing Control" system used in Germany, a statement from parent company Schenker-Rhenus AG said.
No introduction date for the system was given.
Jochen Smoktun, airfreight director of SI Germany, told a recent company airfreight managers meeting in South Africa that seven-figure sums could be saved in this area alone.
Schenker International will also practise closer quality control of airlines and monitor flight schedules more intensively to improve air cargo shipping, the statement said.
Schenker International is the air and sea freight forwarding division of Schenker-Rhenus, which is part of the Stinnes trading group.
